newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's lending rate 40 bps higher at 11.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's lending rate 40 bps higher at 11.4 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate ended 40 basis points higher on Friday at 11.4 percent, lifted by more term loans and a 50-point rise in the call money rate.
Dealers said stronger demand pushed settlements up to 68.1 million kuna from Thursday's 24.2 million.
The daily trade left a shortage of some 12 million kuna for the first time in days since liquidity improved due to a central bank cut in reserve requirement.
Fresh call money deals, accounting for 48 million of the total, were struck at 10.5 percent again.
Banks paid 10.5 and 14 percent for short-term kuna of up to five days.
Insurers rolled over one-week funds at a steady nine percent, and banks charged 15-17 percent for one-two month interbank kuna, depending on borrowers.
The central bank's kuna midrate for Saturday and next Monday eased to 6.1497 against the dollar while firming to 3.5736 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
